intro.objective: Solve a linear equation that needs a single step. Use the inverse operation to undo what has been done to the unknown, doing the same to both sides to keep the equation balanced.
commonMistakes: Only changing one side — whatever you do to one side you must do to the other.
Using the wrong inverse: the inverse of × 3 is ÷ 3, not − 3.
For x ÷ 4 = 3 you multiply both sides by 4; do not divide.
Sign slips with negatives — for example, x + 7 = 2 gives x = −5, not 5.
methodSteps: Step 1: Look at what has been done to the unknown letter.
Step 2: Choose the inverse operation that undoes it.
Step 3: Apply that inverse to BOTH sides of the equation.
Step 4: Simplify each side to get the letter on its own.
Step 5: Check by substituting your answer back into the original equation.
workedExample: Step 1 — 7 has been added to x.

methodReminder: 1  See what was done to the letter
4  Simplify to leave the letter alone

frame: A number has been added to the letter — undo it by subtracting the same number from both sides.
For x + 5 = 12, subtract 5 from each side: x = 12 − 5.
Here the letter has been multiplied or divided.
For 4x = 20, the inverse of × 4 is ÷ 4: x = 20 ÷ 4.
For x ÷ 3 = 6, the inverse of ÷ 3 is × 3: x = 6 × 3.

questions.content:
Solve. The letter is on the right this time.

   a) 9 = x + 4
   b) 20 = 5x
   c) −8 = x − 3

Form an equation and solve it.

   a) A number n is multiplied by 4 to give 28. Find n.
   b) When 5 is subtracted from a number p, the result is 12. Find p.

A rectangle has width w cm and length 5w cm.
The length is 35 cm.

   a) Write an equation in w. (1 mark)
   b) Solve it to find the width w. (1 mark)
   c) Work out the perimeter of the rectangle. (1 mark)

A delivery company charges the same fixed price £x for each parcel.
Four parcels cost £26 in total.

   a) Write an equation for the total cost. (1 mark)
   b) Solve it to find the price of one parcel. (2 marks)
   c) A customer has a £40 budget. What is the greatest number of whole parcels they can send? Show your working. (2 marks)
